rationale: The parent configuration question's recorded account still carries a limitation that the child multi-voter question has now answered: it said the nonvoter addition kept the quorum at one voter and that a voter-adding change a stale configuration would miscount was not witnessed, and that multi-voter election consequences were argued from the code. The child question has since established exactly that, with four complete comparisons and controls (configuration loss in a five-voter cluster, minority leadership, single-side and two-sided acknowledgement). This update revises the parent's limitation list to point at that witnessed evidence instead of leaving the stale wording, keeps its own comparisons and receipts unchanged, and adds the child's receipts with joint history. Nothing else about the parent's account changes: its own witness (empty rebuilt configuration, index restored, hasVote false) stands, and the startup-blocking and authority questions are untouched.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a restarted node that keeps a stale smaller configuration can both win leadership on a minority of the committed configuration and acknowledge client writes concurrently with the majority side's own leader: in one execution both sides acknowledged a client write while partitioned, and the flag-off control acknowledged only on the majority side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader before either write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: The parent question is answered by receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) with receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 as the earlier execution of the same declaration: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node reported after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored (event index 1, versus the admission at index 0 recording before_latest_index 1 with one server), and the flag-off control kept index 1 with one voter (event index 3). The snapshot-present case in the same receipt shows the loss with a committed membership change newer than the snapshot: before shutdown the log's latest configuration was index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sat at index 1220 with configuration index 1, and after the restart the node reported after_latest_index 1 with one server (event index 5, admission 4). Mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:604-620) is the only other, but restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped; processLogs forwards them to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The follow-on child question has since witnessed the multi-voter variant that this account previously listed as an open limitation: with a five-voter committed configuration and a three-voter snapshot the restarted node came back at index 1 with three servers (receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, witness index 15, control 18), and that stale configuration let it win leadership and acknowledge client writes on a minority of the committed configuration, including concurrently with the majority side's leader (receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c, witness index 27, control 29).
counterevidence: The flag-off controls keep the committed configuration in every cited execution, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of its configuration index, which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot.
limitations: The parent's own witness uses a single-voter configuration and a nonvoter addition; voter-adding changes and minority-election consequences are witnessed under the child question, not here.
The stale configuration is observed through the node's own view; no client-visible failure of a single-voter cluster beyond the inability to campaign is measured here.
The startup-blocking and authority questions are separate and not part of this account.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipts 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 and 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 are the parent's own executions of the same single-voter scenario (the second being the earlier execution of the same declaration before identity fields were corrected); receipts b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 and f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c belong to the child multi-voter question and are cited here only for the follow-on consequence named in the revised limitations. All four are complete executions over the same stores and sizes, and each is a self-contained history rather than a fragment of another.
